subject: Service disruption: model inference slowdowns — leadership notice & commitments
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amira Cohen <amira.cohen@nimbus.ai>, ops@nimbus.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Action] Degraded inference throughput impacting Nimbus models

Hi Amira / Nimbus ops team,

Quick note to confirm we are seeing a sustained degradation in model inference throughput starting ~08:45 PDT for the models you run on our dedicated fleet (model-family: rwd-7b-q4). Some customer requests are timing out or returning delayed completions. We have elevated to SEV-2 and opened an incident channel. Karthik and David are on the bridge; I am looping in leadership for executive visibility.

What we know so far:
- Impact: requests over a subset of GPU hosts show token generation latency spikes of 3x-6x.
- Scope: ~12% of requests routed to the affected pool; others are healthy.
- Symptoms: high kernel queuing and increased memory churn leading to throttling.

Immediate actions in flight (teams + ETA):
- Autoscale surge to warm standby capacity (in progress) — ETA 20m (David)
- Routing policy update to steer traffic away from affected hosts — ETA 15m (Karthik)
- Tracing + log collection for root cause (in progress) — ETA 40m (Neha)

We will post periodic updates to this thread and to the Jira ticket below. Please confirm if you observe anything different on your side (additional error types, client-side timeouts) and whether you want us to pause inference traffic from a subset of your API keys while we remediate.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Amira Cohen <amira.cohen@nimbus.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, ops@nimbus.ai
Cc: Tomasz Zielinski <tomasz@nimbus.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:28:04 -0700
Subject: Re: [Action] Degraded inference throughput impacting Nimbus models

Neha — thanks for the quick heads up. We are seeing elevated 504s in our prod integrations and several customer dashboards are alerting.

Questions:
- Any ETA on when routing changes complete?
- Will there be any data loss or dropped requests we should be prepared to reconcile?
- If you need us to throttle client traffic from our side, we can do so but would prefer a targeted key pause rather than broad rollback.

We rely on the rwd-7b-q4 family for our real-time enrichment path; this window is high impact. Please keep us posted and we appreciate the clear owner list.

—Amira
Amira Cohen
Head of Product Operations, Nimbus Analytics
amira.cohen@nimbus.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amira Cohen <amira.cohen@nimbus.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, ops@nimbus.ai
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 10:05:30 -0700
Subject: Re: [Action] Degraded inference throughput impacting Nimbus models

Amira — routing change completed at 09:56 PDT. Summary of work and immediate customer-facing commitments we are making now: 

What we did:
- Shifted Nimbus traffic off the affected GPU pool to warmed standby (non-disruptive) — this has brought average latency for your keys back to baseline for ~88% of traffic.
- Identified several hosts with abnormal kernel queue depth; those hosts have been cordoned for detailed investigation.
- Applied a short-lived conservative batching cap for rwd-7b-q4 to reduce memory churn while we root-cause.

Customer-facing commitments (executive summary):
- Short-term mitigation: routing and batching cap deployed to restore service to the majority of your traffic — completed.
- ETA for full remediation: 36–48 hours to complete host-level forensic, kernel upgrade, and staged return to normal batching profile. We will accelerate if root cause is isolated to a single kernel/driver combo.
- Credits: we will issue a usage credit proportional to the measured request impact window; ops and billing will follow up with the exact calculation within 3 business days.
- Postmortem: we will run a joint postmortem review with Nimbus within 7 business days and share a technical writeup and remediation timeline.

Deliverables we will provide in next update (by 13:00 PDT):
1) Initial forensic notes and the support-log-snippet.txt (attached).
2) A mitigation timeline PDF outlining the steps and anticipated rollback plan.
3) A proposed postmortem agenda and invite for a joint review.

If you want us to throttle specific API keys while we finish the host investigation, tell us the key suffix and we will apply a targeted policy.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amira Cohen <amira.cohen@nimbus.ai>, ops@nimbus.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Action] Degraded inference throughput impacting Nimbus models

Amira / Nimbus team —

Thanks for the quick signal. Brief update and commitments from Redwood leadership side: 

1) Current state: routing change restored baseline performance for ~88% of your traffic. A narrow subset of customer flows still experience intermittent latency — we are cordoning 4 hosts and running kernel-level diagnostics.

2) Customer impact mitigation: we will keep the conservative batching cap in place until kernel patch validation completes. If you prefer an alternative (targeted key-level throttling), we can enact it immediately — let us know the key suffix and we will apply.

3) Compensation: as noted, Redwood will provide usage credits. Ops will calculate a precise credit and send formal confirmation by Tuesday EOD.

4) Postmortem and follow-up: I am scheduling a joint technical postmortem for next Wednesday, 10:00 PDT (calendar invite attached). We will deliver a public-facing summary and a technical root-cause writeup within 5 business days. The postmortem-scope.md is attached and outlines the agenda items and data requests we need from Nimbus.

Attachments included in this thread: support-log-snippet.txt (sample logs), mitigation-timeline.pdf, postmortem-scope.md

Jira: https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/browse/RI-8421
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xNimbus-Incident-20270509

If anything changes on your side or you want us to expand the executive outreach list, flag it here and we will escalate. We appreciate your patience while we close this out.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
